title: feat: install gh CLI + jq + python3 in runner image
body:
## Summary

Adds `gh`, `jq`, and `python3` to the runner image so workflows can use GitHub CLI and JSON parsing without relying on `apt-get install` at runtime.

## Problem

Workflows running on `[self-hosted, builder-org]` fail with `exit 127 gh: command not found`. Example: [netbox-wg Gemini PR Review run 25850846317](https://github.com/Majowka/netbox-wg/actions/runs/25850846317) — `Check PR author association` step couldn't run `gh pr view "${PR}" --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft'`.

The base `ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:latest` image is minimal and does NOT include `gh` (or `jq`). Hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners do — workflows authored against GitHub-hosted runners often assume these tools exist.

## Fix

Adds standard `apt-get install` for the three tools to the existing `RUN` block structure:

```dockerfile
RUN ... \
    && apt-get install -y gh jq python3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

`gh` from official cli.github.com debian repo (signed). `jq` and `python3` from default debian repos.

## Impact

Affects every workflow using `[self-hosted, builder-org]`. After image rebuild:
- Gemini reusable workflows in `Majowka/.github` start working end-to-end
- Other workflows that previously needed `gh`/`jq` install-on-fly can drop that step
- Image size grows by ~50MB (gh = ~15MB, jq = ~1MB, python3 = ~30MB)

## Test plan

- [ ] Build & push image (auto-triggered on Dockerfile change per build workflow)
- [ ] Verify `gh --version`, `jq --version`, `python3 --version` work in a test workflow run on `[self-hosted, builder-org]`
- [ ] Re-run failed Gemini PR Review on netbox-wg — should now pass `Check PR author association` step
